# Deai Canvas — instructions for agents

This folder is a Deai Canvas space: a folder with a `space.json` (name, colour, enabled modules and their settings),
the space's tasks and, optionally, its own modules in `modules/<id>/`. Deai Canvas is a local canvas where a designer
sees the mockups an agent writes, compares iterations and leaves comments.
Everything between the `deai:begin` and `deai:end` markers is generated by Deai Canvas and replaced when Deai Canvas
updates: do not edit it, write your own notes above or below it.

## Getting started

The canvas runs on this computer, by default at `http://127.0.0.1:8765` (the interface is at `/app/`). If it is not
running, start it with `python3 <deai>/app/serve.py`; `<deai>` is the folder of the Deai Canvas installation, so ask
the designer where Deai Canvas is installed. If the canvas runs on another port, use the address shown in the designer's
browser instead of `8765` in every URL below.

When the canvas is running, ask it where it is installed:

    GET http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/agents-md?space=<id>

The answer has `paths.deai`, `paths.inbox` and `paths.authoring`. The same paths are shown in Settings → AGENTS.md in
the canvas. Spaces are listed by `GET http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/spaces`, tasks of all spaces by
`GET http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/tasks?all=1`.

Create a task:

    POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/task-new {"id": "<task-id>", "title": "<title>", "space": "<id>", "from": "/abs/path"}

`from` is optional: an absolute path to a folder with an `index.html`, which becomes the first iteration.

## Tasks and iterations

- A task is a folder that keeps its versions as iterations: `iterations/it1/`, `iterations/it2/`, … Each holds the
  pages (`<page>/index.html`). The designer compares iterations in the canvas.
- Iterations are registered in the task's `iterations.json`. To add one, ask the canvas; it copies `itN` into a new
  iteration:

      POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/iteration {"from": "itN", "note": "what this iteration is"}
      header: X-Canvas-Task: <task-id>

  A folder created by hand is not registered and does not show in the canvas.

## Comments

The designer pins comments on the mockup. Read the open ones and resolve them:

    python3 <deai>/bin/inbox.py
    python3 <deai>/bin/inbox.py --task <task-id>
    python3 <deai>/bin/inbox.py resolve <comment-id> --reason "what you changed"
    python3 <deai>/bin/inbox.py --task <task-id> resolve <comment-id> --reason "what you changed"
    python3 <deai>/bin/inbox.py reply <comment-id> --text "question or note"

`--task` names a task of this space instead of the current one (use it when several sessions work in parallel). A
reason is required: it is what the designer reads.

People's replies under a pin are part of the task: read them with the comment. When the meaning of a comment is
ambiguous, ask in its thread with `reply` instead of guessing; a reply on a team pin is visible to colleagues. Write
`--text="..."` when the text starts with a dash.

## Modules

A module gives the space one role:

- `publish`: publishes marked iterations as a preview link.
- `tokens`: brings the design-system tokens in.
- `comments`: shares comments with the team.
- `vcs`: git sync, sends an iteration to a repository and pulls changes back as a new iteration.
- `dashboard`: the team dashboard, a shared board of the team's task cards.
- `tracker`: shows a task's status from an issue tracker (read-only).
- `notify`: sends a notification to a chat for every new comment.

To connect one, every call takes the space `<id>`:

    GET  http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/modules?space=<id>
    POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/module-enable   {"space": "<id>", "id": "<module>", "settings": {}, "secrets": {}}
    POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/module-check    {"space": "<id>", "id": "<module>"}
    POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/module-settings {"space": "<id>", "id": "<module>", "settings": {}, "secrets": {}}
    POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/module-disable  {"space": "<id>", "id": "<module>"}

`modules` lists the catalog with each module's settings (secrets only as set or unset). `module-enable` turns a module
on with its settings and secrets, `module-check` asks the module whether it works. `module-settings` changes them:
omit a key to keep it, `null` deletes it. `module-disable` turns the module off and keeps its settings. Secrets go only
through the `secrets` field and stay on this computer.

Own modules live in `modules/<id>/` of this space; see `<deai>/docs/modules/authoring.md`. Their code does not run
until a human trusts the module in the canvas. With `"api": 2` a module can also add tools to the island (a panel in a
sandbox) and actions (⌘K and the menus of a task or iteration); details are in the same document, a working example is
`<deai>/docs/modules/examples/page-notes/`.

## Settings

The gear in the canvas opens Settings: the space (name, colour, folder), its modules, and this file.

## Never

- Do not put secrets (tokens, passwords, keys) in this folder: it is shared through git.
- Do not edit `space.json` by hand: use Settings or the module API.
- Do not create iteration folders by hand: use `POST /api/iteration`.
- Do not ask the canvas to trust a module: only a human can.
